title: 3. Use a Clear and Engaging Story Structure
use_cases: Use when drafting the initial outline for a serialized web novel
Implement when planning chapter-by-chapter pacing and story milestones
Configure when determining the placement of the midpoint climax and resolution
Use when balancing character development with plot-driven tension
content:
Before you start writing a web novel, you should have a plot set aside to help you on this journey. This is a very important aspect of your work. If you want your readers to engage with what you have written, things need to go accordingly — the scenes need to pop up at the right time, and everything has to fall into place the more you write & the more they read. The best web novels follow a structure that maximizes engagement. A simple formula would be:

- Setup (Chapters 1–10): Establish the protagonist, main conflict, and stakes.
- Rising Tension (Chapters 11–40+): Introduce twists, deepen conflicts, and build emotional stakes.
- Midpoint Climax (Chapters 40–60+): A major turning point where everything changes.
- Final Conflict & Resolution (Last 20 chapters): Deliver the emotional payoff and satisfying ending.

Each chapter should move the plot forward while keeping character relationships and conflicts evolving. Now, do note that you don’t have to follow this structure of setting everything between Chapters 1–10, 11–40, etc. You can decide when to bring in the tension & the climax. The above is just meant to give an illustration.
